newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile takes another look at Colbun bid.
newsitem.headline: Chile takes another look at Colbun bid.

text.p: Chile could sell 37.5 percent of state electrical utility Colbun to a Belgian-Spanish-Chilean group after all, the government said only two days after rejecting its offer as too low.

Chile's state companies authority CORFO said it would leave open the possibility of selling to the consortium, as long as the bidders agreed to pay CORFO's asking price and respect Colbun's current contracts "in their essence."
"The government has agreed to maintain the possibility of awarding the shares to that consortium," said CORFO in a statement.
The statement strongly suggested there were some contacts going on between the government and the consortium, made up of Powerfin, Iberdrola SA and local firms Minera Valparaiso SA and Enagas SA.
Both the consortium's bid and Colbun's asking price are secret. But CORFO spurned the sole bid in an auction Tuesday, saying it fell below the shares' market value.
About 85 percent of Colbun is state-owned and the rest trades on the Santiago Stock Exchange. The company is Chile's last state-controlled electric power company.
CORFO also said the two sides would have to reach a final agreement by next Wednesday for the sale to take place.
